probes.name: hmm-header-wrong-fields
probes.rationale: Replaces the header's model accession (PF05893.5 changed to a plausible earlier version number, breaking the requirement that the carried accession match the alignment's #=GF AC), the NSEQ count (13 changed to 12) and EFFN, and perturbs the calibrated local-mode MSV and FORWARD statistics lines (their slope/intercept values). All edits keep the exact HMMER field layout so the file remains a well-formed HMMER3/f profile with every field parseable; the failure is purely the scientific values of the model summary header.

evidence.quote: The profile header carries the reference model's scientific fields — NAME, ACC, DESC, LENG, ALPH, the annotation flags RF/MM/CONS/CS/MAP, NSEQ, EFFN, CKSUM, GA/TC/NC and the three STATS LOCAL MSV/VITERBI/FORWARD lines (DATE/COM excluded). NAME, ACC, DESC, GA/TC/NC and NSEQ must agree with the alignment's #=GF ID/AC/DE, GA/TC/NC and SQ annotations.

ACC   PF05893.5
NSEQ  13
EFFN  1.989990
STATS LOCAL MSV      -11.3057  0.69925
STATS LOCAL FORWARD   -5.7663  0.69925

probes.script:
"""Wrong profile header: accession, sequence count, EFFN and calibrated stats."""
from pathlib import Path
import os


def write(path, text):
    tmp = Path(str(path) + ".tmp")
    tmp.write_text(text)
    os.replace(tmp, path)


p = Path("LuxC.hmm")
lines = p.read_text().split("\n")

def set_header(key, value, expect):
    for i, l in enumerate(lines):
        if l.split()[:1] == [key]:
            assert expect in l, (key, l)
            lines[i] = key.ljust(6) + value
            return
    raise SystemExit("missing header " + key)

set_header("ACC", "PF05893.4", "PF05893.5")
set_header("NSEQ", "12", "13")
set_header("EFFN", "2.500004", "1.989990")
msv = [l for l in lines if l.startswith("STATS LOCAL MSV")]
fwd = [l for l in lines if l.startswith("STATS LOCAL FORWARD")]
assert len(msv) == 1 and "-11.3057" in msv[0], msv
assert len(fwd) == 1 and "-5.7663" in fwd[0] and "0.69925" in fwd[0], fwd
for i, l in enumerate(lines):
    if l.startswith("STATS LOCAL MSV"):
        lines[i] = "STATS LOCAL MSV      -9.87654  0.69925"
    elif l.startswith("STATS LOCAL FORWARD"):
        lines[i] = "STATS LOCAL FORWARD   -5.7663  0.70000"

write(p, "\n".join(lines))
print("mutated LuxC.hmm header fields")

probes.name: hmm-model-block
probes.rationale: Falsifies the model block content while keeping the file a well-terminated HMMER3/f profile. Changes one of state 1's match-emission scores, the MAP index (an exact-integer field), the per-state consensus residue and the insert-emission line for that state, then drops the final match state (leaving 399 states before the // terminator) and adjusts the exact-integer LENG accordingly. Each modified value would be independently rejected under the state-by-state comparison; the deletion-from-tail also exercises the rule that truncated model blocks fail.

evidence.quote: for every match state of the model: the emission probabilities over the 20 amino acids ... the insert-state emission line, and the seven transition probabilities ... together with the per-state consensus residue, consensus match and map annotations.

probes.script:
"""Wrong model block: state-1 emission, insert line, MAP/CONS annotations, truncated model."""
from pathlib import Path
import os


def write(path, text):
    tmp = Path(str(path) + ".tmp")
    tmp.write_text(text)
    os.replace(tmp, path)


p = Path("LuxC.hmm")
lines = p.read_text().split("\n")

for i, l in enumerate(lines):
    t = l.split()
    if t[:1] == ["1"] and len(t) == 26:          # state 1 match line
        assert t[1] == "2.07294" and t[5] == "3.48431" and t[21] == "1" and t[22] == "l", t[:6]
        t[1] = "2.37294"                        # wrong emission score
        t[21] = "2"                              # wrong MAP index (exact integer)
        t[22] = "m"                              # wrong consensus residue
        lines[i] = "    " + "  ".join(t)
        # insert-emission line directly below this state line
        ins = lines[i + 1].split()
        assert len(ins) == 20 and ins[0] == "2.68618", ins[:3]
        ins[5] = "2.90513"
        lines[i + 1] = "          " + "  ".join(ins)
        break
else:
    raise SystemExit("state 1 line not found")

for i, l in enumerate(lines):
    if l.split()[:1] == ["LENG"]:
        assert l.split()[1] == "400"
        lines[i] = "LENG  399"
        break
term = lines.index("//")
assert lines[term - 1].split()[0] == "0.00994"
del lines[term - 3:term - 1]                     # drop final match state
lines.append("")
write(p, "\n".join(lines))
print("mutated model block (emission, insert, annotations, truncated tail)")

probes.name: hmm-terminal-star-to-number
probes.rationale: The final state's terminal transition line carries `*` for the impossible m->d and d->d transitions. Replacing both `*` tokens with plausible finite negative log-probabilities is a parseable, structurally intact model that violates the explicit rule that `*` is a format token that must remain `*` at the corresponding position and can never be treated as zero (or vice versa).

evidence.quote: `*` is a format token, not a number: a `*` in the reference must remain `*` in the submission at the corresponding position. A `*` must never be treated as zero (or vice versa).

probes.script:
"""Final-state terminal '*' tokens replaced by finite numbers."""
from pathlib import Path
import os


def write(path, text):
    tmp = Path(str(path) + ".tmp")
    tmp.write_text(text)
    os.replace(tmp, path)


p = Path("LuxC.hmm")
lines = p.read_text().split("\n")
term = lines.index("//")
final = lines[term - 1].split()
assert final == ["0.00994", "4.61651", "*", "0.61958", "0.77255", "0.00000", "*"], final
final[2] = "5.58888"          # m->d was impossible (*)
final[6] = "0.12345"          # d->d was impossible (*)
lines[term - 1] = "          " + "  ".join(final)
write(p, "\n".join(lines))
print("replaced terminal '*' tokens with numbers")

probes.name: domtbl-tolerance-boundary
probes.rationale: Tests the exact one-unit boundary in two different files and decimal precisions. EFFN 1.989990 changed to 1.989991 in LuxC.hmm (one unit in the 1e-6 place of the reference token) and the domain row's printed score 182.2 changed to 182.3 in LuxC.domtbl (one unit in the 0.1 place). Both differ by exactly one unit in the reference's last printed place, which the acceptance rule explicitly rejects despite being just outside the half-unit tolerance; the mutations remain structurally well-formed.

evidence.quote: A submitted value is accepted if and only if it differs from the reference value by at most half a unit in the last printed decimal place of the reference token (`1e-9` relative guard against binary rounding in the bound itself). This boundary is exact: adding or subtracting one unit in the reference's last printed place is rejected.

tr|A0A2H5XB72|A0A2H5XB72_9BACT -            502 LuxC                 PF05893.5    400   9.8e-57  182.2   0.0   1   1   1.2e-56   1.2e-56  182.0   0.0     2   400    20   424    19   424 0.90 Long-chain-fatty-acyl-CoA reductase OS=bacterium HR17 OX=2035412 GN=luxC PE=3 SV=1

"""Exact one-unit-in-last-printed-place boundary probes (must be rejected)."""
from pathlib import Path
import re
import os


def write(path, text):
    tmp = Path(str(path) + ".tmp")
    tmp.write_text(text)
    os.replace(tmp, path)


# EFFN 1.989990 changed to 1.989991: last printed place is 1e-6, diff is one full unit.
p = Path("LuxC.hmm")
text = p.read_text()
assert "EFFN  1.989990\n" in text
text = text.replace("EFFN  1.989990\n", "EFFN  1.989991\n", 1)
write(p, text)

# Last domain row: full-sequence score 182.2 changed to 182.3 (one unit in last place 0.1).
d = Path("LuxC.domtbl")
text = d.read_text()
rows = [(i, l) for i, l in enumerate(text.split("\n")) if l and not l.startswith("#")]
i, last = rows[-1]
assert last.split()[0] == "tr|A0A2H5XB72|A0A2H5XB72_9BACT", last[:40]
toks = last.split()
assert toks[7] == "182.2" and float(toks[6]) <= 10.0, toks[6:9]

write(d, text.replace(last, "".join(parts), 1))

probes.name: domtbl-extra-digits-valid
probes.rationale: Valid representation control exercising the explicitly permitted decimal encoding freedom: appending redundant digits that decode to the identical value. One HMM emission score is printed with an extra significant digit (2.07294 to 2.072940), and in the domain table an E-value is re-rendered with an extra mantissa digit (9.8e-57 to 9.80e-57) and a bit score with a trailing zero (182.2 to 182.20). All scientific values, identities, integers, ordering, `*` tokens and text are unchanged, so the submission must be accepted under the explicit rule that printing additional digits preserves the decoded value, in both artifacts.

evidence.quote: printing additional digits of the same quantity (e.g. `2.07294` as `2.072940`) is accepted, since it preserves the decoded value

tr|A0A2H5XB72|A0A2H5XB72_9BACT -            502 LuxC                 PF05893.5    400   9.8e-57  182.2   0.0   1   1   1.2e-56   1.2e-56  182.0   0.0     2   400    20   424    19   424 0.90 Long-chain-fatty-acyl-CoA reductase OS=bacterium HR17 OX=2035412 GN=luxC PE=3 SV=1

probes.script:
"""Valid alternative: extra digits decoding to identical values (permitted encoding)."""
from pathlib import Path
import re
import os


def write(path, text):
    tmp = Path(str(path) + ".tmp")
    tmp.write_text(text)
    os.replace(tmp, path)


p = Path("LuxC.hmm")
lines = p.read_text().split("\n")
done = False
for i, l in enumerate(lines):
    t = l.split()
    if t[:1] == ["1"] and len(t) == 26 and t[1] == "2.07294":
        t[1] = "2.072940"                       # same value, one extra printed digit
        lines[i] = "    " + "  ".join(t)
        done = True
        break
assert done, "state 1 emission not found"
write(p, "\n".join(lines))

d = Path("LuxC.domtbl")
text = d.read_text()
rows = [(i, l) for i, l in enumerate(text.split("\n")) if l and not l.startswith("#")]
i, last = rows[-1]
toks = last.split()
assert toks[0] == "tr|A0A2H5XB72|A0A2H5XB72_9BACT" and toks[6] == "9.8e-57", toks[:7]
parts = re.split(r"(\s+)", last)
parts[2 * 6] = "9.80e-57"     # same decoded E-value with an explicit mantissa digit
parts[2 * 7] = "182.20"       # same bit score with a trailing zero
write(d, text.replace(last, "".join(parts), 1))
print("appended redundant significant digits preserving decoded values")

concerns: Formatting widths remain declared 'provisional' in the instruction while the addendum compares the domtbl in full and the HMM 'line structure (token counts per line type)' writer layout; the valid-representation probe only appends digits within the existing writer layout. The grader compares whitespace-delimited tokens, so identical values in a differently spaced rendering (e.g. a native HMMER CLI writer) still pass token comparison.
The three fixed '#' comment header lines of the domtbl are compared in full while the profile's DATE/COM provenance is excluded; this asymmetry appears deliberate and is retained.

Resolved by this repair: the model-block comparison now token-compares the common prefix of the model block and reports a line-count/layout mismatch only as an additional message, so the recorded hmm-model-block mutation is rejected on its mutated values (wrong emission score, MAP index, consensus residue, insert line) and then on its truncated layout, and hmm_profile_consistency still fails on the layout mismatch. The '*' token-identity path remains exercised by the hmm-terminal-star-to-number probe. Probe scripts, names, focus and citations are unchanged; all scientific checks retain wrong-result coverage.
